provenance.what: Retrieval parity of the PRE-DEQUANTIZED fp32 query embedder (scripts/predequantize_embedder.py) against the shipped 8-bit model, measured with scripts/verify_embedder_parity.py over the real corpus vectors (data/processed/embeddings/*.parquet, 3152 vectors) and 60 questions (benchmark.json + examples.json). All four pre-registered gates (docs/v2/M5_DECISIONS.md section 2.1: cosine mean >= 0.998 and min >= 0.997, top-1 identical >= 0.95, mean top-8 overlap >= 0.97) pass. The fields below this block are the report exactly as the script wrote it; no metric was changed.
provenance.origin: A scratch experiment of 2026-10-08 (not a CI run), made on Windows 11 / AMD64 with onnxruntime 1.29.0, four threads, against the local single-file model models/qwen3-embedding-0.6b-q8/model_q8.onnx.
provenance.edits_to_the_original_report: Only the path-valued fields were shortened (the original held absolute scratch-directory paths): candidate, corpus_glob and question_files. Nothing else differs.
provenance.scope: This report covers the LOCAL q8 -> fp32 pair named below. An image built with EMBEDDER_VARIANT=fp32 starts from the 8-bit model the Docker model stage quantizes itself, whose source hash may differ; that build is covered only by the in-build gates of scripts/predequantize_embedder.py (every node bit-exact against onnxruntime's own dequantization, read back from the written sidecar, plus the 53-question cosine gate against its 8-bit source). The output does not depend on how the source stores its weights: the same local 8-bit model rewritten into the Docker layout (graph + model_q8.onnx_data, a different source hash) produced byte-identical fp32 files.

candidate_build.same_bytes_as_the_experiment: The experiment built its candidate with an ad-hoc script. The repo script was run on the same source afterwards and produced byte-identical files, so this report describes the repo script's output.

not_measured: Linux RSS and timing, and anything on Fly (a later Fly window will measure both).
Peak memory of the build-time cosine gate on the Docker/Fly remote builder (the gate holds a 2.3 GB session).
Bit-exactness is a property of the build machine's onnxruntime dequantization; the build re-checks it on every build.
